title: To be with artificial intelligence in oral test or not to be: a probe into the traces of success in speaking skill, psychological well-being, autonomy, and academic buoyancy
extended_summary:
This paper asks whether AI-powered tools, specifically ChatGPT, can improve EFL learners’ speaking performance and also influence related non-cognitive outcomes such as psychological well-being, learner autonomy, and academic buoyancy. The authors frame the study as addressing a gap in research on the broader effects of AI in language assessment, beyond simple test scores.

The intervention involved using ChatGPT to score and provide feedback on speaking responses in TOEFL iBT speaking tasks. Participants first completed a Michigan Language Proficiency Test to confirm upper-intermediate proficiency, then took a TOEFL iBT speaking pretest, practiced speaking with ChatGPT feedback, completed an immediate posttest, and finally a delayed posttest three weeks later. Psychological well-being, autonomy, and academic buoyancy were explored through narrative frames, making the study concurrent mixed-methods.

The sample consisted of 28 upper-intermediate EFL students from a university in Ethiopia. Quantitative results showed significant gains in speaking scores from pretest to posttest and delayed posttest, with retention of improvement over time. Qualitative findings suggested that ChatGPT reduced anxiety, increased motivation and confidence, supported self-directed learning, and helped students cope better with academic challenges. The authors conclude that AI-assisted oral assessment can support both language development and learner well-being, though they note limitations related to the small, single-site sample and reliance on self-reported qualitative data.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed mixed-methods study, but it is not a randomized controlled trial and uses a single intact class (n=28) without a clear comparator. The qualitative outcomes are informative, and the quantitative speaking analysis is within-subject only, so causal credibility is limited.
impact_tier_rationale: The speaking outcome shows a large improvement (partial eta squared=0.770) with sustained gains at delayed posttest, which exceeds the threshold for medium/large impact. Although the sample is small and context-specific, the magnitude of the observed speaking gains is substantial.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT used as an AI-assisted tool for scoring and providing personalized feedback on EFL oral speaking tasks in TOEFL iBT speaking practice.

finding.finding_summary: Speaking scores improved substantially after ChatGPT-supported oral practice. In the 28 upper-intermediate EFL learners, mean TOEFL iBT speaking scores increased from 5.214 (SD=2.024) at pretest to 16.071 (SD=4.936) at immediate posttest and remained elevated at 15.357 (SD=4.676) at delayed posttest. The repeated-measures analysis showed a significant time effect (Wilks’ lambda=0.230, partial eta squared=0.770), indicating a large improvement that was largely retained three weeks later.
finding.measure: TOEFL iBT speaking section scores at pretest, immediate posttest, and delayed posttest
finding.std_deviation: Pretest SD=2.024; posttest SD=4.936; delayed posttest SD=4.676

finding.finding_summary: Qualitative narratives indicated improved psychological well-being after using ChatGPT for oral test feedback, especially reduced anxiety, increased motivation, and higher self-confidence. Participants reported that the nonjudgmental, immediate feedback created a more supportive learning environment, but the study did not provide a quantitative effect size for this outcome.
finding.measure: Narrative frame themes on psychological well-being (anxiety, motivation, self-confidence, supportive environment)

finding.finding_summary: The qualitative findings suggest that ChatGPT increased learner autonomy by promoting self-directed practice, individualized learning, confidence in independent practice, and resourcefulness. Participants described being able to practice speaking anytime and use instant feedback to manage their own learning, but the paper reports no quantitative effect size for autonomy.
finding.measure: Narrative frame themes on learner autonomy (self-directed learning, individualized learning, independent practice, resourcefulness)

finding.finding_summary: The study’s qualitative analysis also found positive effects on academic buoyancy, including greater fortitude, problem-solving, perseverance, and adaptability in speaking tasks. Learners reported feeling more able to handle speaking tests and recover from difficulties, though the study did not report a quantitative estimate for this construct.
finding.measure: Narrative frame themes on academic buoyancy (fortitude, problem-solving, perseverance, adaptability)
